narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 28% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. In practical terms, among 100 applicants with a similar profile, about 28 would be expected to run into serious repayment problems; that estimate was above the lender’s approval cutoff, so the application was declined.

The most influential factor was your credit history. It was ranked first and, in this assessment, actually leaned toward good credit rather than bad, even though your history is recorded as critical or other credits. The second most influential factor was having an existing bank installment plan. Only about 8.7% of approved applicants have that, and it pushed the decision toward bad credit. The third factor was the requested loan duration. Your 12-month request is shorter than the approved average of about 19 months, and that pushed toward good credit.

Although two of the three strongest factors worked in your favor, the bank installment plan was a meaningful warning sign, and other less influential information combined to keep your overall estimated risk at 28%, above the cutoff.

To improve your position, ask the lender for the specific reasons on your file, check your credit report for errors, bring any overdue accounts up to date, and reduce existing installment obligations before reapplying. A smaller request or waiting until your credit history and savings look stronger may also help.
